grades.quote: When A=0, this PMP entry is disabled and matches no addresses.
grades.reason: Explains how a PMP entry's A field (OFF/TOR/NA4/NAPOT) determines which addresses the entry matches. This is the matching part of the decision. It does not cover priority, access size, or R/W/X permission checks.

grades.quote: Each PMP address register encodes bits 33-2 of a 34-bit physical address for RV32
grades.reason: Describes the PMP CSR layout and the pmpaddr encoding of physical address bits. This is background on the registers. It says nothing about how an access is matched or permitted.

grades.quote: Only access types configured in the PMP rule matching the requested address range are allowed; failures will cause an access-fault exception.
grades.reason: Smepmp introduction that defines terms such as PMP rule, Enforced, Denied, and Locked. It gives only auxiliary context on what enforcement means. It does not explain the matching or permission decision itself.

grades.quote: When the L bit is set, these permissions are enforced for all privilege modes. When the L bit is clear, any M-mode access matching the PMP entry will succeed; the R/W/X permissions apply only to S and U modes.
grades.reason: Explains how the L bit controls whether R/W/X permissions apply to M-mode versus S/U-mode accesses that match an entry. This is a key part of the permission decision. It does not cover entry priority or access size.
